title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 3–11. New: CISA added six vulnerabilities to the KEV catalog on Nov. 10, including Cisco BroadWorks, two Barracuda bugs due Nov. 13 that require forensic triage, Openwave, Microsoft Outlook, and Chromium. The Nov. 9 entries, including OpenSSH, remain due Nov. 12 and still require forensic triage. SonicWall CVE-2026-19868 remains due Nov. 20. Apple CVE-2024-27834 remains due Nov. 18. No CISA KEV alert dated Nov. 11 was found.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: an OpenSSH and musl bug can accept a long string as an empty password
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 5 that a combined OpenSSH and musl libc bug can let someone into Alpine, and into other distributions where the conditions are set, by typing more than 256 characters at the SSH password prompt. It said the bug works when a system user has an empty password, which it said is the default on multiple distributions, and that Alpine ships with those conditions and with password authentication enabled. It said the bug is present, though not necessarily enabled, on Buildroot, Yocto, and Void Linux, and that OpenWRT uses Dropbear by default. Tom's Hardware said most of these systems are not reachable from the internet, and that an attacker already inside a network, or holding one valid account, could scan for the condition.

items.headline: CISA and the FBI warn that attackers are changing refrigeration-controller settings
items.summary: A Nov. 5 joint fact sheet from CISA, the FBI, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Agriculture, and the Department of Transportation says the agencies are aware of malicious activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems globally. The fact sheet says actors are targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold-storage facilities, and that they may use authentication bypass, code injection, or weak configurations on unpatched or internet-accessible devices. It says a successful change of settings can force continuous heating and defrost cycles, with effects that include inventory loss, a fire hazard, and loss of temperature visibility. The agencies told owners to take controllers off the public internet, isolate operational-technology devices, change default passwords, patch firmware, and alert on setpoint deviations.

items.headline: Singapore CSA: PHP2Shell is being chained to root Palo Alto firewalls, and F5, Cisco, and Citrix are also affected
items.summary: Singapore's Cyber Security Agency said Nov. 3 that active exploitation of PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, has been reported against Palo Alto Networks firewalls running affected PAN-OS versions, targeting internet-exposed management interfaces. The agency said attackers have also been observed chaining those bugs with Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300, which it calls Fragnesia, to gain root after the initial compromise. It said PHP2Shell also affects selected products from Cisco, including Duo Access Gateway and Expressway Series; Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway; F5 BIG-IP APM and the BIG-IP Configuration utility; and Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices running affected PAN-OS. The agency told administrators to apply vendor updates, restrict management interfaces to trusted networks, and look for unauthorized access and persistence.

items.headline: CISA adds Cisco, Barracuda, Openwave, Outlook, and Chromium bugs to KEV
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 10 it added six vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: CVE-2026-20320 in Cisco BroadWorks, CVE-2026-111560 and CVE-2026-116606 in Barracuda Networks products, CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder, CVE-2026-124194 in Microsoft Office Outlook, and CVE-2026-125350 in Google Chromium. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 13 for both Barracuda entries and requires forensic triage; it says the command-injection bug and the email-gateway authentication bypass can be chained. The other four are due Nov. 24, do not require forensic triage, and list ransomware use as unknown. CISA said the BroadWorks bug could let an unauthenticated remote attacker read configuration information, the Outlook bug could allow spoofing over a network, and the Chromium bug could allow code execution inside the sandbox via a crafted webpage, including in Chrome, Edge, and Opera.

items.headline: CISA adds GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, OpenSSH, and IBM Aspera bugs to KEV, due Nov. 12
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 9 it added four vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: CVE-2026-102895 in GPUStack, CVE-2026-116779 in SignalWire FreeSWITCH, CVE-2026-123158 in OpenSSH, and CVE-2026-123218 in IBM Aspera Faspex. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 12 for each, requires forensic triage, and lists ransomware use as unknown. It says the GPUStack bug could allow unauthenticated administrative access, the FreeSWITCH bug could allow code injection, the OpenSSH bug on Linux could allow authentication bypass, and the Aspera Faspex bug could let an authenticated user bypass authorization and escalate privileges. CISA said this type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector and poses significant risk to the federal enterprise.

items.headline: CISA adds a SonicWall SSL VPN authentication bug to the KEV catalog, due Nov. 20
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 6 it added CVE-2026-19868, a SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN use-of-single-factor-authentication vulnerability, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The catalog says the bug may let a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method bypass SAML authentication controls, and that successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 20, does not require forensic triage, and lists ransomware use as unknown. CISA said this type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector and poses significant risk to the federal enterprise.

items.headline: CISA adds an Apple pointer-authentication bug to the KEV catalog, due Nov. 18
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 4 it added CVE-2024-27834, an Apple improper-authentication bug, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The catalog says Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS, and watchOS 10.5 contain a flaw that could allow an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability to bypass pointer authentication. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 18, does not require forensic triage, and lists ransomware use as unknown. CISA said this class of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector and poses significant risk to the federal enterprise.

items.headline: CISA, the NSA, and Australia publish questions on vendor post-quantum readiness
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 5 that it, the Australian Signals Directorate's Australian Cyber Security Centre, and the National Security Agency released joint guidance and a quick-reference list for assessing whether vendors are ready to move to post-quantum cryptography. CISA said widely used public-key cryptography will be vulnerable to a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, and that many organizations depend on vendors for managed services, cloud, and devices that are hard to update, including industrial control systems and Internet of Things products. CISA said the questions are vendor-neutral and are meant to show whether a vendor understands the risk, can account for where cryptography is implemented, and can support a transition. The page points readers to CISA's post-quantum cryptography initiative for further material.

items.headline: Federal News Network: Brian Mazanec is acting head of CISA infrastructure security
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Nov. 3 that Brian Mazanec is serving as acting executive assistant director for infrastructure security at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and that CISA said he was sworn in Monday. The outlet said he was previously deputy assistant secretary and director of the Center for Preparedness in the Department of Health and Human Services' Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, and that he stepped down last week after serving there since January 2023. Federal News Network said that at HHS he helped lead the response to the Change Healthcare ransomware attack, and that CISA wrote he had partnered with CISA and the FBI on joint cybersecurity advisories. It said the infrastructure security division secures critical infrastructure from all hazards and provides risk assessments, tools, and training.
